questions.why: Selects the implementation/runtime contract before code is generated.

questions.prompt: What kind of page is this?
questions.why: Prevents a standalone LP from being forced into a company theme pattern, or vice versa.

questions.prompt: How should existing repository architecture be treated?
questions.why: Determines whether existing CSS/JS/template/component conventions are authoritative.

questions.prompt: How editable should content be from the CMS?
questions.why: Visual repetition alone must not decide CMS ownership.
Controls field capabilities and deliverables without silently assuming ACF Pro.

questions.prompt: How should repeated-looking content be modeled?
questions.why: Visual repetition is evidence, not automatic permission to create a Repeater.
Avoids turning one page into an unnecessary page-builder architecture.
Reference widths are evidence; intermediate widths are a separate robustness problem.

questions.prompt: How should widths without a Figma reference be handled?
questions.why: Prevents blindly reusing breakpoints from another project.

questions.prompt: What is the desktop/mobile asset policy?
questions.why: Avoids replacing authored PC/SP compositions with an assumed shared crop.

questions.prompt: Which representation is authoritative for Figma visuals?
questions.why: Separates editable text from authored identity, vectors, masks, and composites.

questions.prompt: How should slider/carousel behavior be decided?
questions.why: A slider-looking Figma frame does not prove autoplay, loop, drag, navigation, or pagination.

questions.prompt: What is the visual fidelity reference?
questions.why: Pixel fidelity needs a concrete reference; robustness states must not be diffed against nonexistent Figma states.

questions.prompt: Should CMS mutation robustness be required?
questions.why: Separates Figma baseline fidelity from edit/add/remove/reorder robustness.

questions.prompt: What ACF field-definition deliverable is required?
questions.why: Prevents PHP templates from being delivered without reproducible field definitions.

questions.prompt: What level of human editability is required after AI implementation?
questions.why: High fidelity must not silently produce code that humans cannot safely maintain.

questions.prompt: Are there explicit implementation prohibitions or protected areas?
questions.why: Captures constraints such as V2/V3 protected paths, existing class names, libraries, or template ownership.
